title: 西洋建築史
subtitle: History of Occidental Architecture
teachers:
KATSUHARA Motoki
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: This course aims to provide students with a historical understanding of several style characteristics and aesthetic compositions of the architecture that form the cities and regions of the West, originating from ancient Oriental architecture to modern periods. This course also aims at understanding of spatial characteristics of each architectural style, technical features of each historical period that fulfilled the requirements of use, function and structure, as well as the philosophy and social background underpinning them.
advice:
1. Ancient Oriental architecture, Ancient Greek architecture, Hellenistic architecture
2. Ancient Roman architecture
3. Early Christian Architecture and Byzantine Art and Architecture
4. Romanesque architecture
5. Gothic architecture
6. Medieval city
7. Renaissance architecture and architects (15th century)
8. Mannerist Architecture (16th Century)
9. Baroque architecture, Rococo architecture
10. Neoclassicism and 19th century architecture
11. The origin of modern design
12. Development of modern and contemporary architecture
books: 有名建築事典：イラスト＆解説500[学芸出版社]
requiredKnowledge: Use Google Earth etc. to understand the geographical relationship of the architecture mentioned in the lecture, and read books and architectural magazines to get in touch with the latest trends.

activityGoals.body: To obtain an overview of the historical development of Western architectural design.
To perceive morphological characteristics of styles in each period and to identify them.
To understand the relationship between architectural uses, function and structure as well as its expression.
To think critically about things from a variety of perspectives, including historical approaches.

achievementLevels.ideal: To understand the purpose and meaning of studying the history of architecture, and to develop the ability to understand and briefly explain the developmental process of architectures and cities in each region and period, relevant qualitative changes in space and the ideals and social background underpinning them, and to think about the subject matter, meaning in “Architecture”, while maintaining a basic knowledge of the history of Western architecture.
achievementLevels.standard:
To acquire a basic knowledge of the history of Western architecture necessary for taking the Ikkyu-kenchikushi examination, with exploring major trends in Western architecture, names for elements in ancient to late architecture, and names of architects.
To understand architectural characteristics in each period (style, construction method, material, decoration, idea of architects, social background, etc.) and to acquire the ability to analytically understand and appreciate architecture according to its basic design and external feature.

              This course aims to provide students with a historical understanding of several style characteristics and aesthetic compositions of the architecture that form the cities and regions of the West, originating from ancient Oriental architecture to modern periods. This course also aims at understanding of spatial characteristics of each architectural style, technical features of each historical period that fulfilled the requirements of use, function and structure, as well as the philosophy and social background underpinning them.
